newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INTERVIEW-IP IN NO RUSH FOR CHH.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-IP IN NO RUSH FOR CHH.

text.p: International Paper vice president David Oskin said IP was happy with its stake of just over half of Carter Holt Harvey Ltd and had no immediate plans to go to 100 percent.
"As far as our positioning is concerned and where we are at, we quite happy with what we've got right now," Oskin, an IP representative on the CHH board, told Reuters.
Oskin, a former CHH chief executive, agreed there were a number of IP assets that were now in 100 percent ownership and just a few that were not.

"Clearly back in 1995 when we moved to 50 percent, it was a pretty large investment, so at this point we are happy," he said after CHH's annual meeting. "We are just not interested, at this point (in a full takeover)," he said.
IP is in the middle of a restructuring involving the sale around US$1.0 billion in assets, which will involve the loss of around 9,000 jobs.
Oskin said he was confident CHH's legal wrange with Compania de Petreolos de Chile (Copec) would turn in CHH's favour. CHH owns 30 percent of Copec.
"Maybe things haven't moved on as quickly as we would have liked, but we are as patient as can be," he said.
CHH's dispute lies with Chile's Angelini Group, which controls Copec and which has prevented CHH from taking a greater role in its management. The matter is under arbitration.
